title: Debt and Asset
premise: Sable Whitlock, a disgraced intelligence analyst haunted by a night in Vienna she can't fully remember, is approached by a man claiming she saved his life—a favor she has no memory of performing. He repays it by warning her that her name sits atop an assassin's list, tied to a leaked financial instrument that could collapse European markets at Frankfurt's opening bell. Hunted across three capitals and unable to trust her own fractured recollections, Sable must reconstruct the truth of the incident from fragments, informants, and one hostile government's buried files. In the end she exposes the scheme minutes before the markets open, but the cost is devastating: the memory she recovers reveals she was complicit, and survival means living with what she chose to forget.
about_author: Felix Thackeray is the pen name of a former financial-crimes investigator who spent a decade inside compliance departments on three continents before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people who know exactly how systems fail because he's watched them do it.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Insomniac and blacklisted, Sable works dead-end contract gigs until a stranger named Ilya corners her outside a laundromat, thanking her for saving his life in Vienna—something she cannot recall doing—and warns her someone is paying to have her erased. The beat: dread cracking open a carefully managed numbness.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Ilya explains the debt: a shell fund called Meridian Veil moves money for three governments, and a document naming its architects lists Sable as a source. He gives her a burner phone and forty-eight hours before the assassin, known only as Corvus, reaches London. Beat: reluctant re-engagement with a world she fled.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, No Alibi
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. She tests old contacts; each agency denies knowing her, yet all three quietly flag her passport within hours. Someone with reach wants her findable—or gone. Beat: paranoia sharpening into focus as she realizes her exile was engineered.

chapters.title: Corvus
chapters.summary: POV: The assassin. Corvus reviews the Whitlock file and notices an anomaly: the kill order predates the Vienna incident by six days. Professional curiosity becomes a liability for his employer. Beat: cold competence laced with the first thread of doubt.

chapters.title: The Night She Can't Remember
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Under pressure, Sable's fragmented memories surface: a hotel bar, a courier bag, blood on a stairwell—but the sequence won't assemble. She realizes her insomnia began the night her memory ends. Beat: terror of not trusting her own mind.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens at Nine
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Decoding the Meridian Veil ledger fragment, she learns the full scheme detonates when markets open Friday morning: a coordinated short against three sovereign bonds, masked as a counterterror operation. Beat: stakes crystallize from personal to systemic.

chapters.title: The Man from Section Nine
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. A British handler, Deverell, offers protection in exchange for the ledger—but Sable recognizes his questions are mapping what she knows, not who wants her dead. She escapes his safehouse through a service corridor. Beat: loyalty to institutions dies for good.

chapters.title: Ilya's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Ilya. Ilya's own chapter reveals he isn't what he claimed: he was the courier in Vienna, and Sable did save him—by taking the blame for a theft he committed. His repayment is genuine; his guilt is corrosive. Beat: sympathy complicating deception.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe Truth
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Hiding in Rotterdam, Sable and Ilya compare accounts of Vienna and find a four-hour gap both their stories share. Something happened in that gap that neither remembers—and someone paid heavily to bury it. Beat: uneasy alliance built on mutual damage.

chapters.title: What Corvus Found
chapters.summary: POV: Corvus. Following the money backward, Corvus discovers his own agency bankrolled Meridian Veil, and his previous two contracts were witnesses. He begins keeping evidence instead of erasing it. Beat: the hunter becoming a target.

chapters.title: Berlin Station
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. A German BfV archivist, Marta, agrees to pull the sealed Vienna file—for a price: Sable's testimony against a minister involved. The file exists but requires clearance Sable can only get by walking into a trap. Beat: bargaining away safety for truth.

chapters.title: The Gap
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. A hypnotherapist and chemical trigger recover a sliver of the missing hours: Sable didn't just witness the theft—she negotiated it, trading the ledger's existence for her own career resurrection. Beat: self-recognition as the story's cruelest turn.

chapters.title: Complicit
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Shattered, Sable nearly surrenders to Deverell, believing she deserves the bullet. Ilya forces her to see the choice she faces now versus the frightened analyst she was then. Beat: rock bottom and the first ember of resolve.

chapters.title: Corvus Closes
chapters.summary: POV: Corvus. Corvus finds them in Rotterdam but hesitates—his file now proves Sable is a loose end, not a threat. He offers a trade: her evidence for his testimony. Beat: enemy becoming reluctant ally.

chapters.title: Deverell's Web
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Reassembling the conspiracy, they map all three governments' fingerprints on Meridian Veil—and realize Deverell orchestrated the leak to trigger the market crash himself, using Sable as the fall analyst twice over. Beat: the true villain revealed.

chapters.title: The Minister's Price
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Marta delivers the sealed file but is compromised; a raid scatters the group, and Ilya is taken. Sable must choose between extracting him and reaching the Bundesbank whistleblower who can freeze the trades. Beat: loyalty versus mission, made literal.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: POV: Ilya. Interrogated by Deverell's people, Ilya gives up nothing that matters and engineers his own escape using the same routes he used in Vienna. Beat: redemption earned through endurance.

chapters.title: Night Before the Bell
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. The team converges in Frankfurt: Sable, Ilya, and Corvus, an assassin guarding the woman he was sent to kill. They plan to push the evidence simultaneously to regulators, press, and a parliamentary committee at 8:00 a.m.—one hour before open. Beat: calm before detonation.

chapters.title: Eight O'Clock
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. The release goes live, but Deverell counterattacks, triggering a warrant branding Sable a foreign agent. Regulators waver; one outlet bites. Corvus draws Deverell's security detail away at terrible cost. Beat: climax igniting on every front.

chapters.title: The Tower
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Confronting Deverell in the ECB tower's data center, Sable uses her recovered memory—the recorded negotiation from Vienna—as leverage, proving his authorship. Markets open on the news; the shorts burn. Beat: truth deployed as a weapon.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Three governments scramble, Deverell vanishes into diplomatic fog, and Sable testifies under immunity—confessing her own complicity publicly. Her name is cleared; her sleep is not. Beat: victory shadowed by accountability.

chapters.title: Sleep Through the Night
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. Months later, Sable sleeps eight hours for the first time since Vienna, then wakes and chooses to keep working—not hidden, but visible, rebuilding analysis on her own terms. Ilya sends a postcard: debt paid. Beat: hard-won peace without absolution.
